title: Negative actions: singular partitive object
summary: Choose singular partitive objects in supplied negative action statements.
objectives: Choose singular partitive objects in supplied negative action statements.

sections.title: Meaning and pattern
paragraphs: Choose singular partitive objects in supplied negative action statements.
The object names what the action concerns. The negative verb carries the person ending; the main verb is supplied without one. Change only the object case.
This rule concerns an object. A noun identifying someone after a form of be has another job; do not transfer this rule to every negative statement.
keyPoints: In this straightforward negative statement, the object uses singular partitive. Negation does not make every noun in every sentence partitive.

examples.english: I do not buy a car.
steps: In this straightforward negative statement, the object uses singular partitive. Negation does not make every noun in every sentence partitive.
En means “I do not” and works as the verb. en comes from ei: the first-person singular negative verb en.
osta means “buy” and works as the verb. osta comes from ostaa: the negative main-verb form osta-, without a person ending.
autoa means “car” and works as the singular partitive noun used as the object of the action. Add -a to auto: autoa. The ending is selected from the word’s back vowels.

examples.english: I do not see a book.
steps: In this straightforward negative statement, the object uses singular partitive. Negation does not make every noun in every sentence partitive.
En means “I do not” and works as the verb. en comes from ei: the first-person singular negative verb en.
näe means “see” and works as the verb. näe comes from nähdä: the negative main-verb form näe, without a person ending.
kirjaa means “book” and works as the singular partitive noun used as the object of the action. Keep kirja and add -a: kirja + a = kirjaa.

examples.english: I do not buy a cup.
steps: In this straightforward negative statement, the object uses singular partitive. Negation does not make every noun in every sentence partitive.

osta means “buy” and works as the verb. osta comes from ostaa: the negative main-verb form osta-, without a person ending.
kuppia means “cup” and works as the singular partitive noun used as the object of the action. Keep strong pp and the final i: kuppi + a = kuppia.

examples.english: I do not see a ball.
steps: In this straightforward negative statement, the object uses singular partitive. Negation does not make every noun in every sentence partitive.

palloa means “ball” and works as the singular partitive noun used as the object of the action. Keep pallo unchanged and add -a: palloa.

commonMistakes: Keep the supplied negative verb frame intact.
Do not treat a subject or identity noun as an object.
